metadata.title: Bihar Chhath Puja, Finale Day 4 - Bhoriya Aragh / पारन I Akshaya/Amla Navmi + Kerav & Satvik bhojan
metadata.description:
On the last day of chhath puja at the break of dawn, we ventured towards the ghat, eagerly looking forward to experiencing the sacred rituals of Bhoriya argh. The was alive with devotion as families, clad in their finest attire, arrived laden with offerings. Spirits were high as everyone eagerly awaited the rising sun, armed with prayers and offerings. As rays of the sun began to appear in the horizon, the fasting women, including Svaita ji, immersed themselves in the river waters to perform the bhoriya argh and other rites. The entire atmosphere was buzzed with excitement, reverence and a shared sense of joy palpable among all present.

After the puja rituals, we partook of prasad. Upon returning home, Svaita ji, who had fasted throughout the ceremony, broke her fast with gud, tulsi leaves and ginger, followed by a simple yet satisfying meal consisting of rice, dal, dried peas curry and potato fry. As she concluded her meal, the rest of the family partook in theirs, marking the end of the Chhath Puja festivities. This experience served as a profound opportunity to encounter tradition and devotion. We proffer our heartfelt thanks to Savita Ji and her family for welcoming us so warmly and allowing us to celebrate the festival with everyone. 

Additionally, a few days later, we had the privilege of participating in the Akshay Navami Puja within our locality. This ceremony reveres the Indian gooseberry tree as a symbol of Lord Vishnu and Lakshmi adding another layer of spiritual richness to our cultural exploration.
